label: Acceptance
description: Prove the product deliverables (not the units): can the person from the story actually get the value? (feature.md §6). classify routing out of the phase is a rule about classify and the refine loop a rule about critique, so each sits on its own mount; the root reads finding_class to decide where the run resumes.

## What a later phase sent back

{{.inputs.findings}}

A phase downstream of this one found the work does not hold up
where they stand — which is why control came back here. That is a different reader
from your own critique: they are looking at what your output made possible, not at
whether it is well made. Fix what they name, or say plainly why they are wrong.

**Re-emit the deliverables in full.** What you produced above is superseded — the
complete set comes back, not a diff — and `responses` carries one entry per finding
above, in the same order, on the contract the brief already gave.

The docs you opened are still open. Re-read only what a finding above puts in question,
or what another state may have edited since; re-reading the rest is the largest single
cost of a refine pass and it buys nothing.

Write one acceptance test per deliverable. These prove the **product
deliverables**, not the units.

Phase 5 already defended every phase-4 invariant with a unit test beside the code.
Nothing here repeats that. This phase asks the only question those tests cannot:
**can the person from the story actually get the value?**

## How to write them

**Walk the flow's steps** and assert the **success signal** — the observable the
flow declared as "the person got the value".

The test that matters is the one that fails when the person stops getting the
value. So before you write each one, do this: **imagine the feature technically
working and worthless** — the data loads but is wrong, the run starts but never
finishes, the list renders but is empty when it should not be. Does your test
still pass? Then it asserts an intermediate, and you have not written the test
yet.

Rules:

- **Do not mock the thing under test.** What has to be real for this test to mean
  anything — the store, the agent runtime, the file system? Make those real.
  What may still be faked, fake.
- **Do not take a shortcut the person cannot take.** Reaching through the API
  when the deliverable is reached through the UI produces a test that passes while
  the real path is broken.
- **Weight coverage toward what breaks silently** — no crash, no error, just
  wrong. Those need the most coverage and usually have the least.
- **Every phase-4 failure mode** should be reachable and observable the way the
  person experiences it. Where one is not, leave it uncovered and say so rather
  than asserting it from the inside.
- **Delete or rewrite tests this feature invalidates.** Do not skip them.

## What to produce

`acceptance_tests` — one row per test: the deliverable it defends, the success
signal it asserts, how it drives the system, what is real and what is faked, and
where the test lives.

`responses` — one entry per finding you were handed above, in the same order, and
nothing at all on a first pass:

```
{ "severity": "significant",
  "claim": "<the finding, as it was put to you>",
  "target_id": "<the id it is about>",
  "disposition": "fixed" | "rejected" | "blocked",
  "note": "what changed | why the finding is wrong | what you would need" }
```

`note` is required for `rejected` and `blocked`. This is the only memory the loop has of
its own passes: the critique reads it to tell an answered finding from a restated one.

Saying you are stuck is a real answer, not a failure. If a finding asks for something
this phase cannot produce — a measurement nobody has taken, a decision only a person can
make, a fact that is not in the repo — mark it `blocked` and name what you would need.
Three passes defending a gap costs more than asking once.

## What the critique said about your last pass

This is a REVISION, pass {{.inputs.iteration}}. Take each finding and
either fix it or say plainly why it is wrong — a finding that comes back
unchanged twice is a finding about this state rather than about the work.

**Re-emit the deliverables in full.** What you produced above is superseded — the
complete set comes back, not a diff — and `responses` carries one entry per finding

## What the person at the gate said

{{.inputs.comments}}

A person read this and sent it back. It is a decision rather than
a critique — they are overriding a recommendation — so what they wrote is the whole of
the reason, and it outranks everything said so far in this conversation.

Re-emit the deliverables in full.

inputs.returned_findings.description: What a LATER phase found wrong with this one, which is why control came back here. Absent on the way down. Shapes differ by sender — a review finding carries `severity`/`claim`/`lens`, a design finding raised by acceptance or implementation carries whatever that phase recorded — so read each entry for what it says rather than expecting one shape.
